subject: Anonymized audit streams: proposed MVP, questions on PII & retention
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Carla Mendoza <carla.mendoza@medisecure.com>, Dave Liu <dave.liu@cloudpartner.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Anonymized audit streams: proposed MVP, questions on PII & retention

Carla / Dave —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap + proposed minimal scope so engineering can size the work: we captured the items we discussed and a handful of open questions where we need your confirmation before we commit to an implementation timeline.

Recap (MVP):
- Deliver an audit stream (Kafka topic) that replicates request/response events for inference calls used in your compliance pipeline.
- Apply deterministic anonymization to PII in payloads: SHA-256 hashing for IDs (customer_id, user_id), token redaction for auth headers, and email obfuscation (username -> hash).
- Strip full request/response body for any field matching the sensitive schema you provided (SSN, full credit card, MRN) and replace with redaction tokens.
- Retention: provide two retention tiers (30d rolling, and 365d archival) with configurable TTL on the topic.
- Data residency: stream origin in us-east-1; if you need EU residency we'll route to a regional topic and provide separate keys.

Open questions (please confirm):
1) For "deterministic anonymization" do you require reversible pseudonymization (HMAC with customer key) or one-way hashing? We recommended one-way hashing for audit streams to avoid key-management complexity.
2) Are trace IDs allowed to persist (hashed) in logs so you can correlate events across services, or must trace IDs be fully redacted
   (i.e., removed from the payload)?
3) Retention policy for indexable metadata (timestamp, model_name, call_duration): confirm whether these can remain unredacted for compliance analytics.
4) Any special regulatory controls (e.g., HIPAA BAAs, encryption-at-rest with specific KMS) beyond what you already listed?

Attachments: redaction-mvp-spec.pdf (proposed schema & sample transforms), audit-streams-playbook-v0.3.docx (operational steps).

Next steps:
- If you confirm Q1–Q3 we will produce a short tech addendum and a 2-week pilot plan (sandbox topic + sample dataset).
- If you require reversible pseudonymization we will surface KMS integration and estimate extra scope.

Thanks — I can set up a 30-min follow-up early next week to finalize.

—
SoojIn Lee
Enterprise Sales (Privacy & Regulated Accounts)
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0184

From: Carla Mendoza <carla.mendoza@medisecure.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dave Liu <dave.liu@cloudpartner.io>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Anonymized audit streams: proposed MVP, questions on PII & retention

SoojIn —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few answers inline below and one additional ask.

Inline: 
1) Hashing vs reversible: we prefer reversible pseudonymization (HMAC with customer-specific key) for internal investigations — however, access to de-pseudonymize should be controlled via a small number of users (Security team). Can Redwood support an optional HMAC mode keyed by our KMS?

2) Trace IDs: we are okay with hashed trace IDs (one-way) for cross-service correlation if the hash is stable and consistent across events. Full cleartext trace IDs are not permitted to leave our tenant.

3) Indexable metadata: timestamp, model_name, call_duration — these are OK to keep unredacted. We will want a sampling knob for full request body (e.g., 0.1% for debugging).

4) Regulatory: yes, HIPAA applies. We will need a BAA and signatures before pilot starts. KMS: we use AWS KMS (alias /aws/redwood/ms-prod) and need to ensure keys never leave our account.

Additional ask: For the pilot can you deliver a small mapping file that shows example inputs -> anonymized outputs (pseudonymized user_id sample set) so our security team can validate the transforms?

I'll loop in our Security engineer (not on this thread) if we move forward.

Thanks,
Carla
Carla Mendoza
Head of Privacy & Compliance
MediSecure Health
carla.mendoza@medisecure.com
(617) 222-3344

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Carla Mendoza <carla.mendoza@medisecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dave Liu <dave.liu@cloudpartner.io>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Anonymized audit streams: proposed MVP, questions on PII & retention

Carla — thanks for the quick clarifications. A few commitments and clarifications below.

- HMAC mode: yes — we can implement an optional HMAC-based pseudonymization where the HMAC key is your KMS-wrapped key. Implementation note: this adds ~2 days of integration work and a one-time security review. We'll call this an optional add-on in the pilot.
- Trace IDs: we will return stable one-way hashed trace IDs for cross-service correlation by default. Hashing algorithm and salt can be provided by you; otherwise we will use SHA-256 with a Redwood per-tenant salt.
- Sampling: we'll add a configurable sampling rate for full request body capture (default 0%).
- BAA & KMS: we can provide a standard BAA. For KMS usage we will integrate using cross-account key policies so keys stay in your account; engineering will produce an architecture diagram in the tech addendum.

Action items (ownership):
- Soojin: deliver tech addendum + pilot plan (target EOD Monday 6/18). Attachment: updated MVP spec will show HMAC flow and sample pseudonymized mapping.
- Rishi (CC): own engineering sizing and confirm estimate (+ any infra asks).
- Marissa: will coordinate legal for BAA and vendor onboarding.

Carla — can you confirm whether the Security engineer needs the mapping in the sandbox (anonymized) or a deterministic reversible mapping in the production pilot? We'll treat mapping distribution as a gated step.

Thanks — I will attach the updated spec after sync with Rishi.

—
SoojIn Lee
Enterprise Sales (Privacy & Regulated Accounts)
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

SoojIn — quick internal note after reading the thread:

- Rishi: please triage INF-2219 (add pseudonymization HMAC option + KMS integration) and give a 2-day spike estimate. Include a short risk list (key rotation, access controls for re-identification).
- Legal: I will start the BAA request with Carla's team; Soojin, please attach the sample mapping artifact only to the sandbox pilot (no production keys).
- Ops/Infra: verify that the retention TTL and separate regional topics are supported in our hosted architecture; if not, flag design changes.

I'll be on the call Monday if needed.

Marissa
